title: Roger Hawkins: The Pulse of Muscle Shoals (Jeff Potter, Modern Drummer, 26 April 2017)
notes: "Most of the time it was Ludwig because I had always dreamt of Ludwig"; tuning "to the song—whatever would fit in with the song and the way the singer was singing"; a finger round the snare to find where to tape it; "don't be doing tom-tom fills when the singer's singing"; "Al Jackson was a big influence. I listened to him a lot"; Jim Keltner and Jim Gordon as players who could cut a track live; Kodachrome, "a loping feel", played with hard vibes mallets on a box with newspaper in it; Old Time Rock and Roll "was just rock 'n' roll like I'd played it a thousand times before"; "I was always a better listener than I was a drummer".

title: Roger Hawkins (Peter B. Olson, Encyclopedia of Alabama, 20 May 2020, updated 6 October 2025)
notes: Born 16 October 1945, Mishawaka, Indiana; died 20 May 2021; demo sessions at FAME and Quinvy; first well-documented FAME session Land of a Thousand Dances, May 1966; founded Muscle Shoals Sound with Jimmy Johnson, Barry Beckett and David Hood in April 1969 at 3614 Jackson Highway; "known for his high-hat inflections, syncopated bass drum work, dynamic snare drum style, and importantly his adherence to the arrangement of the song"; studied Take Five and Mother-in-Law; jazz lessons from Mike Shepherd.

title: Roger Hawkins (drummer) (Wikipedia)
notes: 1945-2021; the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section; Rolling Stone no. 31; the records he is on; his quote on playing with the same four.

title: Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section (Wikipedia)
notes: Hall hired Beckett, Hawkins, Hood and Johnson, the "Second FAME Gang"; Hawkins hired in 1964; the move to 3614 Jackson Highway in 1969; Land of 1000 Dances' drum break; the move to 1000 Alabama Avenue in 1979; closed 1985.

title: Mustang Sally (song) (Wikipedia)
notes: Mack Rice's song, 1965, a 24-bar form; Wilson Pickett's single and The Wicked Pickett, 1966; personnel from The Muscle Shoals Sound: 3614 Jackson Highway, Roger Hawkins drums, Tommy Cogbill bass, Jimmy Johnson rhythm guitar, Chips Moman lead guitar.

title: Chain of Fools (Wikipedia)

title: Lady Soul (Wikipedia)
